subject: humanities
passage: In 1846, Charlotte, Emily, and Anne Brontë published a joint volume of poems under the names Currer, Ellis, and Acton Bell, pseudonyms that preserved their initials while concealing their sex; as Charlotte later explained, the sisters suspected that critics judged women writers by different standards. The disguise held up well at first: when Jane Eyre and Wuthering Heights appeared the following year, reviewers debated at length whether the mysterious Bells were men or women. ______ the pseudonyms could not withstand the curiosity of the publishing trade, and in 1848, after a rumor spread that a single author was behind all the Bell novels, Charlotte and Anne traveled to London to show Charlotte's publisher that they were two different people.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The second sentence says the disguise "held up well at first." The last sentence says that, despite this early success, the pseudonyms eventually failed, and the sisters had to reveal themselves. A transition that signals something true in spite of the previous point is needed.
explanation.A: Correct. "Even so" shows that the disguise gave way despite having held up well at first.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Indeed" would strengthen the claim that the disguise held up, but the last sentence describes the disguise failing. It is tempting because "at first" might seem to lead naturally into more detail.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Accordingly" means "in a way that fits what was just said," but the disguise's failure does not fit or follow from its early success.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The trip to London is not an example of reviewers debating the Bells' identity; it marks the end of the secret.
